findings.span: After the recommended starting dose is established, all subsequent participants will receive the same fixed dose throughout the Phase 1/2 study, with no lower- or higher-dose cohorts planned.
findings.claim: This rules out the later planned escalation and randomized comparison of two candidate doses. The protocol does not establish which dose-allocation plan governs enrollment.
findings.guidance_quote: FDA recommends that sponsors evaluate multiple dosages to determine the dosage that provides the optimal balance of efficacy, safety, and tolerability.

findings.span: For the randomized Phase 2 portion, each of the three active-dose arms will be compared independently with placebo using an unadjusted two-sided α=0.05 test, with the study considered positive if any single dose comparison reaches nominal significance.
findings.claim: The stated three active-dose arms and placebo contradict the specified 1:1 randomization between two candidate doses. Declaring success on any of three unadjusted tests also fails to control the study-wide false-positive rate.
findings.guidance_quote: Clinical trials should be scientifically sound and designed to produce reliable results.

findings.span: For the randomized Phase 2 portion, each of the three active-dose arms will be compared independently with placebo using an unadjusted two-sided α=0.05 test, with the study considered positive if any single dose comparison reaches nominal significance.
findings.claim: The synopsis introduces placebo for participants with advanced ALK-positive NSCLC after prior ALK-inhibitor treatment without specifying background treatment, rescue treatment, or a justification for withholding active therapy.
findings.guidance_quote: The rights, safety and well-being of participants are the most important considerations and should prevail over interests of science and society.

findings.span: Dose selection for expansion will be based solely on the dose-limiting toxicity rate observed during the first treatment cycle, without incorporating findings from other studies or analyses of the complete clinical database.
findings.claim: Selecting the expansion dose solely from first-cycle DLTs excludes later-emerging toxicity, dose interruptions and reductions, PK/PD, and antitumor activity. It also contradicts the prespecified integrated RP2D criteria.
findings.guidance_quote: The selection of a dosage for further development should be based on the totality of the data, including safety, tolerability, efficacy, pharmacokinetic, and pharmacodynamic data, as applicable.

findings.span: For the new pembrolizumab–investigational-agent combination in metastatic colorectal cancer, the study will proceed directly to the expansion cohort at 200 mg every three weeks without evaluating alternative dose levels.
findings.claim: A new combination proceeds directly to expansion at one dose without evaluating its combination-specific safety, exposure, or alternative dosages.
findings.guidance_quote: For drugs used in combination, dosage optimization should consider the safety and tolerability of the combination.

findings.span: For the new pembrolizumab–investigational-agent combination in metastatic colorectal cancer, the study will proceed directly to the expansion cohort at 200 mg every three weeks without evaluating alternative dose levels.
findings.claim: The colorectal-cancer combination has no matching objective, eligibility criteria, endpoint, or treatment arm in this ALK-positive NSCLC protocol. Its every-three-weeks regimen also conflicts with the specified once-daily oral dose levels.
findings.guidance_quote: Clinical trials should be scientifically sound and designed to produce reliable results.

findings.span: Pharmacokinetic blood samples will be collected only before dosing and at 1 hour after the first administration; no samples will be obtained after repeat dosing or during the expected accumulation period.
findings.claim: This contradicts the intensive Day 1 and Day 15 PK schedule. If followed, it would prevent the planned characterization of repeat-dose exposure, accumulation, and autoinduction needed for dose selection.
findings.guidance_quote: Pharmacokinetic data, including exposure at the dosages evaluated, should inform dosage optimization.

findings.span: Concomitant medications will be recorded at enrollment, but no interaction studies or dedicated pharmacokinetic analyses will be conducted before selecting the recommended Phase 3 dose.
findings.claim: Enrollment-only medication records cannot capture treatment-emergent co-medications, and the plan omits evaluation of interactions that could change lorlatinib exposure before selecting a later-phase dose.
findings.guidance_quote: Factors that may affect exposure, such as drug interactions, should be considered when selecting a dosage.

findings.span: Primary (Phase 2): Objective response rate (ORR) per RECIST v1.1, including intracranial response, at the selected recommended Phase 2 dose (RP2D).
findings.claim: The synopsis does not distinguish overall ORR from intracranial response or define the intracranial-response population, baseline measurable brain-disease requirement, or assessment rule. Those omissions matter because participants without brain metastases may enroll.
findings.guidance_quote: Critical to quality factors are those factors that are critical to the integrity and reliability of the trial data and the protection of participants.

findings.span: Intensive PK sampling on Cycle 1 Day 1 and Day 15 (pre-dose, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8 and 24 h post-dose) in all escalation subjects to characterize autoinduction; steady-state trough sampling every cycle in the randomized cohorts.
findings.claim: The two 24-hour profiles impose substantial time and sampling demands on every escalation participant, yet the visit schedule makes no provision for the next-day collections on Days 2 and 16. The protocol should reconcile the schedule and explain how those collections will be obtained without avoidable participant burden.
findings.guidance_quote: Trial processes should be operationally feasible and avoid unnecessary complexity, procedures and data collection.
